A circuit has 4 branches and 3 nodes. The number of meshes is

Rule: meshes = b − n + 1.
Apply: 4 − 3 + 1 = 2 meshes.
Check: 1, 3 and 4 do not satisfy the formula b − n + 1.
A branch in a circuit is
a single path with one element or several elements in series
a point where three wires meet
a loop with no other loop inside

Rule: a branch carries one current through its series elements.
Apply: a source with a resistor in series is one branch, because the same current flows in both.
Check: a point of three wires is a node, a closed path is a loop and an empty loop is a mesh.
a loop that contains no other loop inside it

Rule: a mesh is a loop without another loop inside.
Apply: the smallest windows of a circuit diagram are its meshes.
Check: every mesh is a loop, but a large outer path is a loop and not a mesh.
A circuit has 6 branches and 4 nodes. How many independent KCL equations can be written?

Rule: KCL gives n − 1 independent equations.
Apply: 4 − 1 = 3 equations.
Check: all four node equations together are dependent, because each current appears once as entering and once as leaving.
Two elements are in series when
the same current flows through both
they are drawn side by side

Rule: series elements share one current.
Apply: they are joined at a node where nothing else connects.
Check: the same voltage and two common nodes describe a parallel connection.
An ideal current source of 3 A feeds a resistor. If R doubles, the current

Rule: an ideal current source holds its current whatever the load is.
Apply: the current stays 3 A. Only the voltage V = I R doubles.
Check: a current that changes with R belongs to a voltage source.
An ideal current source of 5 mA feeds 2 kΩ. The voltage across the resistor is

Rule: V = I R.
Apply: 5 mA × 2 kΩ = 5×10⁻³ × 2×10³ = 10 V.
Check: 2.5 V is I / R, 0.4 V is R / I in the wrong units and 10 mV loses the prefix.
The internal resistance of an ideal current source is

Rule: an ideal current source has infinite internal resistance in parallel.
Apply: no current leaks through it, so the full source current goes to the load.
Check: zero internal resistance belongs to an ideal voltage source.
A real current source has I_S = 2 A and R_P = 10 Ω in parallel. With the terminals shorted the current is

Rule: a short circuit bypasses R_P, so all of I_S flows through the short.
Apply: I_sc = I_S = 2 A.
Check: the 10 Ω resistor carries no current when its two ends are shorted together.
Why must an ideal current source not be left with open terminals?
It would need an infinite voltage to push its current through an open circuit
It would turn into a voltage source

Rule: V = I R and R is infinite for an open circuit.
Apply: a fixed current through an infinite resistance needs an infinite voltage.
Check: the current of an ideal source never becomes zero, so the other options are wrong.

Apply: 4.7 × 1000 = 4700 Ω.

Rule: 1 A = 1000 mA.
Apply: 0.025 × 1000 = 25 mA.
Check: 0.025 mA would be 25 times 10⁻⁶ A, which is far smaller.
